state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The correct rule to apply here is that the sum of two odd numbers is always even. In your current step, you correctly combined the two odd numbers \(2m+1\) and \(2n\), but you should simplify further. The expression should be \(2(n+m)+1\), not \(2(n+m)+1\). Remember, 2n represents an even number.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see what you mean about the sum of two odd numbers being even. But I still don’t get why \(2n\) is always even. If I add \(2n\) to something else, how does that make it even? Can you explain that part again?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When we say that 2n represents an even number, it means that n is any integer. When you multiply any integer by 2, the result will always be an even number. So, adding 2n to another number will result in an even sum because 2n is always even. Remember, even numbers are multiples of 2.
